description:
Advances: specled.tag_scanning

TagScanner.process_statement/4 (lib/specled_ex/tag_scanner.ex:255) pattern-matches only @tag, test, and describe nodes; its catch-all silently drops every other AST node — including {:for, _, _}. A test generated by the common ExUnit idiom 'for x <- xs do @tag spec: ...; test ... end' therefore never reaches the tag_map: the tag is not scanned, not even recorded as a dynamic entry. Downstream, tagged_tests stubs covering such ids emit tagged_tests_cover_missing_tag (false positive) and their strength caps at 'claimed', so adopters using the idiom cannot arm missing_tag at :error or strength floors without tripping on tests that exist and are correctly tagged. Demonstrated in Builder (builder-fnl experiment, 2026-08-11): builder.heroku_connect_introspection.workflow_phase_gating had a correct tagged test inside a for-comprehension (test/builder/agent/workflow_phase_test.exs:391-405) and was reported as having no tag carrier; a crude sweep found ~44 for-blocks with spec tags in that one adopter, mostly masked today by duplicate out-of-loop tags. Fix directions: (1) recurse into {:for, _, [..., [do: block]]} bodies in process_statement (the unrolled body contains one @tag + one test — presence is what matters, multiplicity does not); (2) at minimum emit a dynamic_entry instead of dropping, so the blindness is visible. Note prior art: specled_-q59.11 covered list-VALUED tags, a different gap.

Notes:
- Semantics of the threaded accumulator were checked against what ExUnit actually does at
  compile time, not just against the tests. A `@tag` before the loop is consumed by the
  first unrolled test, one inside by the test after it, a trailing one survives past the
  loop — all three match real attribute-consumption order. One asymmetry the code does not
  claim to handle: `test ...` followed by `@tag` *inside* the same body means the tag is
  consumed by the next iteration's test as well as the statement after the loop; the
  scanner attributes it only to the latter. Presence is still recorded, so no
  missing_tag false positive results.
- Entries for for-generated tests carry test_name: nil, because interpolated test names are
  not binaries (test_name_from_args/1, tag_scanner.ex:269). That is pre-existing —
  top-level tests with interpolated names already produced nil — and downstream nil
  handling exists (tag_findings.ex:45-49). Consequence worth knowing: in coverage_closure's
  :per_test mode, strength promotion to "executed" joins on "#{file} :: #{test_name}"
  (coverage_closure.ex:571), which a nil name cannot match, so for-generated tests cap at
  "linked" there. The ticket's stated symptom — capping at "claimed" — is genuinely lifted
  in :aggregate mode (strength becomes "linked" once executed_mfa_count > 0), and the new
  requirement claims nothing about "executed" strength, so this changes nothing about the
  verdict.
- The test file's @moduletag (lines 4-17) blanket-tags every requirement id onto every test
  in the file, a pre-existing pattern in this repo. Per-requirement precision comes from
  the per-test @tag annotations cited above, which do exist for every must requirement.
